text:
Matthew Knies goes back to Toronto on Saturday, and it's not the homecoming either side had in mind a year ago. After 240 games as a Maple Leaf, he has nine points in 19 games for a Columbus team that has lost five straight, and his scoring rate is well below the range we'd expect from him (1.55 points per 60 against about 2.3).

It isn't the finishing. He's shooting right at league average, with four goals on 4.3 expected (the quality of his chances). The problem is volume: the chances just haven't come, and the Blue Jackets take 48% of the expected goals at five on five when he plays. Last season Evolving-Hockey had him at only 0.2 wins, against the toughest competition (97th percentile), with little created offensively while he was on.

He has two goals in his last three games, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking says his offense comes off the rush and from passes behind the net. He's a big body with a hard shot (83rd percentile) and 34 hits already. Watch Saturday in Toronto, where both teams are searching for answers.
